title: Week 4
coldOpen:
One team put up a score that belongs in the record book; another undefeated contender is somehow being punished for making this look too easy; the defending champ went from having too many quarterbacks to needing emergency help; and somebody is now shopping for the exact kind of running back he traded away two weeks ago.

Welcome to the Week 4 PDL Power Rankings.

1: Boy, am I glad that everyone went to tune in to see Delco get absolutely molested for the Game of the Week.
Darren almost outscored me by 100 points.

Philadelphia: 216.16.
Delco: 119.06.
There could have been children watching, Darren.
This is becoming a problem with Delco in general. I keep looking at the names and convincing myself everything is fine.
Lamar Jackson.
Jalen Hurts.
DeVonta Smith.
Jameson Williams.
Josh Jacobs.
Marvin Harrison Jr.
Tyler Warren.
Aaron Jones.
Alvin Kamara.
Mitsubishi Marv followed up last week’s goose egg by roaring back for three catches and 40 yards.
Jacoby Brissett threw the ball 52 times.
Marv got five targets.
Forty-seven passes went somewhere else.
DK at least finally scored a touchdown. He celebrated by firing the football more than 20 rows into the stands and later said the throw was three weeks of frustration coming out.
I have never felt closer to DK Metcalf outside of the fact that we have the same physique.
Jamo gave me another one of those games where I check afterward just to make sure he actually played.
Diggs continues his successful transition from Stefon Diggs to a guy named Stefon Diggs who appears in my starting lineup.
DeVonta was fine.
That is where we are now.
“Fine” is a compliment.
The five receivers I started combined for 37.8 points.
Tyler Shough scored 30.8 by himself on my bench.
Shough threw four touchdowns against Las Vegas.
All four went to tight ends.
Apparently even my backup quarterback has decided wide receivers are a waste of time.
Cooper Kupp also scored 12.6 from the bench, which would have made him my WR1 this week.
I acquired all this receiver depth so I could have more options.
Turns out the option is choosing which guy scores six.
And I can’t even blame some horrific injury luck or a lineup full of zeroes.
Nobody died.
Nobody got pulled after one drive.
Nobody accidentally retired Saturday night.
This was the team.
Just ten recognizable names coming together and making sure nobody had to carry too much of the scoring burden.
Very unselfish football.
I’m 1-2 now.
The six-year playoff streak is still technically alive, although at this point I’m treating it the way NFL broadcasts treat a 38-year-old quarterback returning after three years away.
Nice story.
Didn’t realize we were still doing this.
2: Last week, Connecticut went from 15 points to 28.3, so I projected Joe to keep doubling and score 56.6 in Week 3.
He scored 52.5.
Four points off.
I see no reason to abandon the model now.
Week 4: 105.
The best part is Joe nearly hit the projection without getting a single point from the quarterback position.
Tyson Bagent: 0.00.
Justin Fields: 0.00.
Sam Howell: 0.00.
Mac Jones, Kyle McCord, Quinn Ewers, Jalen Milroe, Drew Allar: you get the idea.
Joe has eight quarterbacks.
They combined for zero points.
And somehow Case Keenum beat all of them.
Darren broke the news on the podcast that Keenum might start against the Eagles, and I thought he had retired and become a quarterbacks coach somewhere.
Nope.

First regular-season action since 2023. 247 yards, two passing touchdowns, another one rushing. Bears win 27-7. Bagent had cleared concussion protocol Sunday, but Chicago still went with the 38-year-old they had sitting behind him.
Thanks for murdering the Birds and ruining my entire Monday.
Joe spent the offseason telling us Bagent could be a guy.
Case Keenum came out of retirement age and said hold on my beer.

At least this clears up one thing from the podcast. We were talking about Joe owning eight 2027 firsts, and Darren pointed out that if he actually used all of them, the board could leave him taking something stupid like five quarterbacks.
Do it. You won't.
I want 13 quarterbacks on this roster.
Maybe then one will play.
Keenan Allen is also still here.
I have spent three straight weeks waiting for somebody to trade for him. A.J. Brown went on IR and I basically packed Keenan’s bags for Wichita myself.
Jeff responded by scoring 188 without him.
So Keenan remains a Connecticut Croc, where he led the team with 15.3*this week and continues to be by far the oldest person involved in Joe’s five-year plan.
Roman Wilson had 13.5. Tre Harris had 10.6. There are at least a couple of young receivers on this roster beginning to resemble NFL players, which is probably enough excitement for September.
The important stuff is still sitting in Joe’s draft tab.
He did make a trade this week, though.
Jameis Winston and Sean McGowan went to Tanish.
Joe got Kimani Vidal and Max’s 2027 fourth.
So Joe actually trimmed the quarterback room and still has eight of them.
More importantly, while the rest of the league is begging him to loosen his grip on one of those 2027 firsts, Joe responded by acquiring another 2027 pick.
A fourth.
Close enough.
Joe can sit there with two-thirds of the first round while the rest of us slowly talk ourselves into offering actual good players for picks we helped turn into gold.
And now he has Max’s fourth too.
Huge week for diversification.
105 next week.
If he actually gets there, I might have to move him to #11.
3: Jeff has a better argument for #1 than I have for putting him at #3.
He is 3-0.
He leads the league at 168.5 points per game.
He scored 188.36 last week and followed it with 174.72 this week.
There is no statistical case against Wichita.
Unfortunately for Jeff, I write this.
And I have decided that “Mike built the best roster I have ever seen” and “Darren just scored 216 fucking points” are metrics now.
So Jeff drops to #3 after winning by 99 points.
He has every right to be mad.
I said after last week’s 188 that it probably wouldn’t be the last stupid Wichita score.
Seven days later, Jeff was sitting at 174 with A.J. Brown still on IR and Saquon giving him 8.5.
All that offseason spending has officially reached the point where I can no longer make fun of it without looking like a hater.
Which is weird because I feel like I am one of Wichita's biggest fans, but I guess the evidence is against me since I ranked them #3 despite all the metrics.
The quarterback room was particularly obnoxious this week because Jeff owned both sides of Steelers-Bengals.
Joe Burrow threw three touchdowns and gave him 28.58. No surprise there, typical Burrow stuff.
Aaron Rodgers was sitting on Jeff’s bench, threw three of his own, scored 27.68, and Pittsburgh beat Cincinnati 30-27. Burrow’s last chance ended with a fumble in the final minute.
Rodgers is 42.
Jeff’s backup quarterback is old enough to remember when Burrow was in middle school and still spent Sunday ruining his afternoon.
Kansas City also keeps turning into Wichita West.
Mahomes.
Kenneth Walker.
Kelce.

All three are on Jeff’s roster, all three are 3-0 in real life, and Walker has apparently become the Tyreek Hill for this Bienemy offense. The Chiefs spent last week talking about potentially managing his workload and then immediately gave him another full afternoon of work while he scored twice against Miami.
Andy Reid heard “limit Kenneth Walker” and treated it roughly the same way Jeff treated “maybe keep some future draft picks.”
No.
Kelce also scored and then credited his fresh haircut afterward, texting his barber that “the fade is giving me powers.”
Jeff has spent so much on this roster that we are now getting production from Travis Kelce’s barber.
I don’t know how to compete with that.
Last week you could at least call 188 an explosion.
Now he puts up 174.
Before that, 142 in Week 1.
There hasn’t been a bad week.
There hasn’t really even been a normal week.
A.J. Brown has barely contributed to the season.
Saquon has already given him a 2.5 and an 8.5.
Jeff is 3-0 and scoring 168.5 a week.
There.

The only reason Wichita is third is because Mike’s roster is starting to look like a Sixers offseason graphic where you have to squint for a minute and figure out how any of this is legal. Darren just produced one of the biggest scores this league has ever seen.
That’s it.
No hidden agenda.
Jeff should probably screenshot this section for when he beats both of them and asks me why I’m such an idiot.
I will have no defense.
4: If you take a gander at Max’s roster, you can come away with:
Needs QB. Surplus WR.
Max’s latest move was trading Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon to Mike for C. Douglas.
Good start.
This also happened less than a week after I spent part of the podcast arguing that Murphy Street might have the best receiver room in the league.

Darren immediately said no because Mike exists. I kept arguing. Eventually I got him to concede top three, and then Darren pulled up FantasyCalc and found Max’s entire roster was actually second in league value, behind only Mike.
Max has spent years accusing the podcast of being against him.
I just spent ten minutes doing free PR for Murphy Street and Max responded by acquiring another receiver.
You’re welcome.
Michael Wilson helped the cause this week with 20.4, narrowly outscoring Ja’Marr Chase’s 20.3.

That’s also the first real receipt Max gets from the Chase Brown trade. Wilson has been on the roster for two weeks and already gave him a 20-point game. I assume Max has that screenshot saved somewhere safe.
The quarterback situation is less settled.
Bryce Young followed his 30-point debut with 14.64.
Stroud had 13.68.
Cam Ward had 10.44 on the bench.
Uh oh.
At running back, Max started Woody Marks and Monangai for a combined 11.7.
Ollie Gordon scored 13 from the bench.
Then Max traded him.
To Mike.
Because Southern Oregon, sitting at 3-0 with the best roster in the league, who acquired Olave last week, apparently needed a little more help.
Mike gets Wright and Gordon.
Max gets another receiver.
Murphy Street finished at 100.02 and lost to Mike 116.64. Max could have pulled off the upset if he kept Kelce and some of the other pieces he shipped away, but the plan is in effect.
At least the direction is pretty obvious now.

Max isn’t trying to squeeze one more run out of the old version of MSE. Dak is gone. Chase Brown is gone. He’s gotten younger, picked up future capital, and keeps taking swings on players he thinks can still appreciate.
MSE down at number 9; end of an era?
5: Jon finally got a week from the 2026 class that didn’t make us immediately ask if he was okay.
Unfortunately, Jeff scored 174.72 against him.
Richmond scored 75.40
So the Reavers found some answers and still lost by 99.32 points.

Last week Darren basically asked on the podcast whether Jon was already getting nervous. Mendoza still wasn’t playing. Lemon had nine receiving yards through two weeks. Tyson and Omar Cooper were hurt. Antonio Williams was probably the best thing Jon had gotten out of the class to that point.
Then Kenyon Sadiq finally did something about it.
Seven catches. 105 yards. A touchdown. 23.5 points. TE4 on the week.
Thank you.
Pat Bryant scored 13.4.
Mike Washington scored 11.4.
Those three combined for 48.3, which is easily the best Sunday Jon has gotten from the guys he actually spent all that draft capital on.
Of course Antonio Williams, last week’s designated bright spot, immediately responded with 2.5.
Nobody gets comfortable in Richmond.
Makai Lemon had 4.4, which brings him to 13 receiving yards through three weeks after opening the season with negative five.

We spent part of the podcast trying to talk ourselves off the ledge with Lemon because it’s obviously early. Then the Eagles brought Zach Ertz back from the retirement home and I immediately started wondering what that says about everybody they already have.
Probably nothing.
Hopefully nothing.
Jon does not need another thing.
Fernando Mendoza still hasn’t given him anything either, mostly because Kirk Cousins keeps refusing to cooperate with the Richmond rebuild.
The Raiders keep winning games. Kirk has been fine. There is no reason for them to hand the offense to Mendoza just because Jon would really appreciate it.
Darren said last week we might not see him until much later in the season. That sounded pessimistic at the time.
It’s starting to sound like Las Vegas does not care about our dynasty league.
Very selfish organization.
And that’s kind of the weird spot Jon is in now.
Sadiq finally popped.
Bryant gave him a real week.
Washington found the end zone.
Those are exactly the things he needed to see.
He’s also 0-3, just got almost doubled up plus another 24 points, and Joe is the only team he outscored this week.
Joe.
The team whose current offensive strategy is mathematical exponential growth.
Richmond beat Connecticut’s score by 22.9.
We are making progress since the Reavers were unable to outscore the Crocs last week.
I’m less worried about Jon’s rookie class than I was a week ago because Sadiq finally gave him a game that actually matters, and Bryant and Washington chipped in behind him.
I am still very interested in what happens if Mendoza stays parked, Lemon keeps doing cardio, and Tyson and Cooper remain unavailable.
Jon bet heavily on this class because he wanted to start seeing the next version of Richmond now.
Week 3 finally gave him a glimpse.
Jeff just buried it under 174 points.
6: Brian is one decent Nico Collins practice report away from doing something stupid.
Last week’s mailbag asked whether Hollywood should move the 2028 first and make a run.
Darren and I both said no. Darren actually went further and said Nico might be the guy Brian should eventually sell because he doesn’t really fit the rest of the roster.
Then Hollywood scored the 5th-highest in the league with 123.40 without Nico.
Of course.
This is exactly the kind of week that gets an owner opening the trade block at 11:30 at night.
Jeremiyah Love looks good.
Bhayshul Tuten looks good.
Parker Washington has me believing that he may be one of the best PSU players right now.
Brian somehow owns enough of the Jaguars' offense that Jacksonville beatingb beating the brakes off of New England 35-6 was good news for him.
And then there is Kirk Cousins.
The Raiders went 2-15 last year.
They are now 3-0.
Kirk is leading the NFL in touchdown passes.
Brian got 28.22 out of him this week while Las Vegas came back from 11 down to beat New Orleans.
Brian does not need encouragement.
Hollywood is 1-2.
He just lost by 43.7.
That should be enough to keep everybody calm.
Unfortunately, the actual roster is starting to give Brian an argument.
The young guys are producing before Nico is even back. Houston has now played two straight games without Collins, and there is at least some optimism that he could return for Week 4.
So I know what comes next.
Nico returns.
Brian looks at a lineup with Jordan Love, Kirk, Nico, Jeremiyah Love, Tuten, Parker, Egbuka, Downs.
He looks at some draft capital he has.
He looks back at the lineup.
Then somebody gets a trade offer at 12:14 a.m.
Please don’t.
And yes, I own Brian’s 2027 first, so I am an extremely compromised source here.
I would like Hollywood to lose every remaining game by one point.
But even taking my personal financial interests out of it, spending another first to chase Mike, Jeff, Darren and Welch right now sounds insane.
Darren just scored 216.
Jeff scored 174.
Welch scored 167.
Mike is 3-0.
Brian’s encouraging week ended with him losing by almost 44.

Jordan Love actually had a pretty fitting Sunday for this team. Green Bay made him throw 53 times for 387 yards and still got smoked 35-14 by Atlanta. Lots of activity. Plenty to point at afterward. Scoreboard still says you got worked.
If this thing is still alive in November, then Brian can start making everyone nervous.
For now, Kirk Cousins being 3-0 with the Raiders is enough delusion for one roster.
7: Darren scored 216.16 points this week.
Fifth-highest score in PDL history.
He could have left Jahmyr Gibbs on the bench and still beaten me by 59.20.
I hate that I know that.
Two weeks ago, Darren was sniffing around the Dak Prescott sweepstakes because quarterback was supposedly the one spot keeping this roster from being complete.
Good thing he showed restraint.
Sam Darnold returned from a glute injury and threw for a career-high 379 yards and four touchdowns. Stafford threw for 390. Deshaun Watson scored 24.26 on the bench.
Turns out the big quarterback acquisition was Sam Darnold getting his ass medically cleared.
Darren is now getting exactly what he wanted from a position he spent the offseason apologizing for.

He identifies the weakness, talks about it for six months, nearly trades for Dak, and then the weakness scores 56 points in one week without him doing anything. Against me, by the way, just in case you forgot.
O.G. TEU also showed up this week. (All those acronyms are probably not the best setup in hindsight)
On the podcast last week, we debuted the “back from the dead” question.
Darren immediately used it to talk about George Kittle.
I accused him, correctly, of hijacking the segment just to discuss his own players.
Then Sunday was literally George Kittle Bobblehead Day in San Francisco.
Eighty thousand Kittle bobbleheads were handed out.
Kittle scored two fourth-quarter touchdowns.
PDL scriptwriters are really picking optimal pain for me this season.
Brock Bowers also came back and scored 27.6 on Darren’s bench.

Jahmyr Gibbs had Barry Sanders in the building for Detroit’s homecoming weekend and apparently took that personally, because he scored three touchdowns and put up 37.9 for Darren. Gibbs said afterward that whenever Sanders is around, he feels like he has to step his game up.
Great.
Darren is now texting Barry to show up when he plays Delco. I can't even take this up to the commissioner for collusion because he's the commish smh.
And somehow, in the middle of all this, Darren’s roster also started breaking.
Baker hurt the thumb on his throwing hand.
Mike Evans left hurt.
Etienne is out.
Njoku and Stowers are already on IR.
That is basically the only argument I have left for keeping Philadelphia out of the top spot.
Because the actual lineup just scored 216.
Darren didn’t catch one ridiculous 50-point outlier.

He had Gibbs go nuts, Darnold return from the glute injury as if nothing happened, Kittle celebrate his own bobblehead giveaway with two touchdowns, and enough production everywhere else that Bowers scoring 27.6 did not even matter.
So congratulations to Darren on the fifth-highest score in league history.
You are still #2 for now.
8: Welch has scored 332.24 points over the last two weeks.
Bucky Irving and David Montgomery combined for 12.6 points this week, and Welch has apparently been asking around the league about a real running back.
Personally, I think a Breece Hall-type would fit this roster perfectly.
Young. Three-down back. Catches passes. Exactly what Dallas needs.
Welch is one good running back away from becoming a legitimate problem.
This is also a very different Welch than we’re used to.
For years, he has been one of the more cautious owners in the league. Every move felt like it needed congressional approval from Oregon.
Now he trades for Dak and immediately starts asking what everyone wants for their running backs.
Growth.
Dak, meanwhile, has already settled into the Dallas Drip perfectly.
His actual Cowboys spent Sunday in Brazil finding a completely new way to lose.

Dallas had first-and-goal at the Baltimore 2 with 23 seconds left, somehow came away with a tying field goal, and still left Lamar enough time to set up a 56-yard walk-off kick. Jerry Jones said afterward there was “no explanation” for the clock management. Brian Schottenheimer gave himself an F.
I'm writing this alone in a hotel room after a long workday, but what I just wrote is straight-up erotica.
Darren said on the podcast that Welch basically has “nothing but a bunch of tight ends.”
Harold Fannin scored twice this week.
Trey McBride gave him another strong game.
Juwan Johnson scored 23.3 on the bench.
Maybe Welch doesn’t need a running back.
Maybe he just needs us to change the starting requirements to four tight ends.
I’m open to hearing the proposal.
Drake London also chose a pretty convenient week to remind everyone why Welch has refused to entertain moving him.

Atlanta spent the first two weeks looking like it had misplaced the red zone entirely. Michael Penix came back Thursday, the Falcons put up 498 yards at Lambeau, and London went for 194 receiving yards in a 35-14 win.
Welch also had Christian Watson on the other side of that game.
So by Thursday night he had already looked like a buzzsaw.
And I’m not going to run through the rest of the lineup because that misses what has changed here.
Welch is actually acting like somebody who thinks he can win the league.
He got Dak.
He’s asking about running backs.
He has now put up 165+ in consecutive weeks.
On the podcast, Darren said one move could turn Dallas from “contender” into legitimate contender.
I think that’s probably right.
9: Greggy had a bye this week.
Bijan and Derrick Henry combined for 55.7.
Joe scored 52.5.
Greg could have started two players and gone home.
Which, based on his general enthusiasm for the 2026 season right now, might have been preferable.
Darren beat him by 60 last week, and Greggy checked out for the season already.
He missed the podcast. He’s down on the season. Herbert looks like Nathan Peterman. The vibes are awful.
Darren beat me by 97 this week, the Eagles got turned into a core childhood memory for Case Keenum’s kids, and I’m still here standing.
Greg gets worked by Darren once and starts mentally checking out?
Weak.
Greg’s problem is that his favorite player on Earth is Justin Herbert, and right now Herbert is doing absolutely nothing to improve the mood.
The Chargers are 0-3.
Their defense forced five Buffalo turnovers on Sunday.
Five.
They still lost 24-16.

Herbert threw a fourth-quarter interception at the Buffalo goal line, the Chargers settled for three field goals on four red-zone trips, and Mike McDaniel’s offense somehow managed to turn five takeaways into another game where scoring 20 points felt impossible.
McDaniel said before the game that the offense was “not standing on business in the least.”
Correct ✅
Greg’s favorite quarterback finished with 13.74 fantasy points.
Bo Nix scored 27.14.
Geno scored 32.04 on the bench.
Justin Herbert finished third in Greg’s quarterback room.

I’m not going to make the obvious joke about Greg loving him anyway because we all know Greg. Herbert could throw four interceptions, lose 13-6, and somehow Greg would emerge from the film session explaining that the third one was actually an elite anticipatory throw.
Last week I was trying to cheer Greg up by talking myself into the Chargers’ upcoming schedule.
Buffalo. Seattle. Denver. Kansas City. Rams. Houston. Baltimore.
My theory was that playing all those good teams might force Herbert into some shootouts and finally get the fantasy production moving.
Buffalo handed the Chargers the football five times, and they scored 16.
And then there is the Rome trade.
I don’t need to go through all 46 offers again. Greg finally got his guy. That part is over.
Here’s the first full-week update:
Rome Odunze: 5.9.
Chris Olave caught nine balls for 107 yards and is now the WR4 on the season.
Southern Oregon is 3-0.

Greg spent years painstakingly building London into a team that could finally win this thing, then celebrated reaching contention by sending his best receiver to Mike because he had been trying to acquire Rome Odunze for so long that the trade had apparently become a hostage negotiation.
I respect following your heart.
I would respect it significantly more if Mike wasn't the main beneficiary of the deal.
Rome will hopefully be great (don't ask Tanish, though). Greg waited two years for him for a reason. I completely understand why he wanted him.
Unfortunately, these are power rankings, and I cannot rank Greg based on how happy the trade made him.
He made his team worse right now.
The league immediately told him that in the mailbag. Darren said the same thing on the podcast.
Then Olave spent another Sunday making the argument himself.
London is still good. Obviously.
Bijan just ran for 194 yards and two touchdowns.
Derrick Henry is still Derrick Henry despite Darren telling me for approximately five years that Derrick Henry was about to die.
Tee Higgins gave him a real week.
Bo Nix looks useful.
Greg scored 134.98 with Herbert doing nothing and BTJ catching one pass.
There are plenty of reasons to believe this team will be there later in the year.
Greg just needs to believe it too.

Right now, he finally owns Rome; Herbert is 0-3; Mike owns Olave; Darren took his lunch money; and Joe conveniently arrived on the schedule before Greg could start listing players on the trade block out of seasonal depression.
Maybe that’s all he needed.
A little time off.
A free win.
Some Rome Odunze highlights.
And absolutely no Chargers football for seven days.
10: Jeff is 3-0 and averaging 168.5.
Darren just scored 216.16, the fifth-highest score in PDL history.
Mike scored 116.64.
Mike is #1.
Welcome to the PDL College Football Playoff committee.
Jeff has the résumé. Darren has the signature win. Mike has the eye test and apparently a permanent spot in my top four regardless of what happens on the field.
I have become everything I hate.

Last week I was already asking on the podcast whether Southern Oregon could become the first team in PDL history to go completely undefeated. Darren reminded me that my old team once went undefeated through the regular season, outscored everyone by roughly 400 points, then got knocked out anyway.
Mike responded to my endorsement by scoring his season low.
For a while Sunday, it looked like Southern Oregon might actually hand me a reason to move him.
Achane tore his ACL on his third carry.
Jefferson left early.
Puka didn’t play.
Josh Allen gave Mike 14.96.
Brock Purdy then scored 39.28.
Mike’s QB2 is now protecting my propaganda operation.
And because Max only scored 100.02, Southern Oregon escaped 3-0 anyway.
The frustrating part of this roster right now might be how quickly the rest of the league keeps fixing it for him.
Greg finally got Rome Odunze after two years of trying and celebrated by sending Chris Olave to Mike.
Then Achane goes down and Max sends Mike Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon for C. Douglas.
That is my entire defense.
Not this week.
I’m looking at the roster.
Pure committee behavior.
If Jeff wants to complain, he should.
He has outscored Mike by nearly 57 points per week over the last two weeks and somehow got moved to #3.
Darren can complain too.
He dropped 216 on me, and I rewarded him by placing him directly behind a team that barely cracked 116.
Maybe this is agenda-driven.
Maybe I decided in August that Southern Oregon was the best team ever assembled in the PDL and now I’m going to need considerably more than one ugly week to admit I was wrong.
Fine.
At least I’m transparent about the corruption.
Welcome to the PDL Power Rankings; it's my world.
11: Brett being 0-3 is fine.
He has been saying for months that he is not trying to win this year.
What sucks is that the guys he actually wants to build around keep getting hurt.

Jackson Dart is now on IR, and the news got worse while we were recording the podcast. We went from a sprained MCL and a few weeks to Schefter reporting that the knee injury was more serious than initially thought and the season could be in jeopardy.
Dart is supposed to be one of the answers here.
Alec Pierce is on IR after reinjuring the same foot he had surgery on.
Jalen Lane is on IR.
Jarquez Coleman is on IR.
Brett also has five empty bench spots right now.
That is a lot of open real estate for a dynasty team.
Trevor Lawrence at least showed up.
24.78 points. Three touchdowns.
Lawrence accounted for almost 30% of Dubrovnik’s entire score by himself, which is probably more responsibility than Brett expected to put on Trevor Lawrence at any point in this rebuild.
Two weeks ago Dart and Lawrence both looked good and Brett had every right to feel a little smug about the quarterback room.
Now Dart is on IR and Lawrence is the healthy one.
Life comes at you fast.
The rest of the young guys were quiet.
Omarion Hampton followed his Week 2 rebound with 5.6.
Tet McMillan had 2.7.
Colston Loveland had 7.1, which is at least enough to confirm he remains alive.
Jordan Addison gave Brett 17.5 and prevented this thing from getting uglier.
Dubrovnik finished with 82.48 and lost to Tanish by 25.
Whatever.
Brett can lose every game this year and it does not change what he is doing.
He already sold Jaden Reed.
He already moved Carnell Tate.
He has been very clear that this roster is not supposed to be ready yet.
The part that matters is whether Dart, Hampton, Tet, Loveland and the rest of the guys he plans on keeping are better in January than they were in September.
Right now Brett has one of them on IR, another giving him five points, another giving him two, and Trevor Lawrence holding the flashlight.
Not exactly how you draw it up.
But if there is one owner in this league who can look at a 0-3 record and genuinely not care, it is probably Brett.
Just stop putting his future on IR.
12: A week ago I said it might actually be a good thing nobody took Tanish up on his months-long attempt to sell one of Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels or Drake Maye.
Six days later he traded with Joe for Jameis Winston.
That market corrected quickly.
Before the season, Boulder had probably the best quarterback room in the league.
Week 3:
Caleb: out.
Jayden: out.
Maye: 1.76 points.
Jameis: 6.12.
Tanish spent all offseason trying to convince everyone he had too many quarterbacks. The league collectively told him to fuck off.
Did we potentially save Tanish's season?
Also, wtf is going on with Drake "The Schedule" Maye?

New England lost 35-6 to Jacksonville. Maye turned it over three times and eventually got pulled for Tommy DeVito after the game was out of reach (I guess you can make the argument that the game was out of reach once it started?)
One of those turnovers was an interception in the end zone.
By Travis Hunter.
Yes.
Tanish used the 1.03 in the 2025 rookie draft on a defensive back, and Hunter’s first career interception came against Tanish’s starting quarterback. *chef's kiss*
The 1.03 finally made a big play for Boulder.
It took points away from Boulder.
I'm literally cracking up as I type this lmao.
And just to make sure there is no confusion here, Tanish did not draft Hunter at 1.03 because he was getting some secret two-way fantasy cheat code.
He drafted a DB.
Third overall.
In a dynasty rookie draft.
Then proceeded to win the league that year.
I have been waiting more than a year for this pick to pay off, and apparently the payoff was making Drake Maye’s 1.76 even worse.

Meanwhile, the Jayden Daniels situation has gone from bad to something Tanish actually has to worry about long-term. Daniels is still expected to try to return this season, but there is now reporting that he could need offseason surgery on the same elbow he has dislocated twice in ten months.
Caleb missed Monday with the hamstring.
So Jameis Winston, acquired from the team intentionally hoarding eight quarterbacks, suddenly became necessary for the defending champion.
Joe finally found a buyer.
It only required two injuries and Drake Maye getting intercepted by Tanish’s own first-round DB.
Fortunately, JSN has apparently seen enough.
